evidence.excerpt: Large pre-trained time-series models have been proposed as general-purpose tools that can be applied to downstream tasks with little or no fine-tuning. This paper benchmarks three recently published time-series foundation models against four classical methods—isolation forest, one-class SVM, ARIMA residual scoring, and a simple rolling z-score—on anomaly detection tasks drawn from five SCADA datasets covering PV parks, a small wind farm, and district heating substations. Evaluation uses a consistent labelling protocol and the same six threshold selection strategies described in earlier work by the same group. Foundation models achieved the highest AUC-ROC on two of the five datasets but were outperformed by isolation forest on the remaining three, particularly where telemetry channels exhibit strong non-stationary seasonality. Inference latency and memory footprint are also reported, as they are relevant constraints for edge deployment in substation hardware.
